profile.address: Halley Street, Google Data Center, Council Bluffs, Lewis Township, Pottawattamie County, IA
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Council Bluffs, Iowa data center campus, mapped along Halley Street in Lewis Township, Pottawattamie County. Google's own locations page for Iowa, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Iowa data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the Council Bluffs campus was the site of Google's original $600 million Iowa investment announced in 2007, and that the company has since invested more than $20 billion in the state; in 2025 Google announced a further $7 billion investment shared between an expanded Council Bluffs campus and a new Cedar Rapids facility. Google reports generating $2.7 billion of economic activity for Iowa businesses in 2025 and training over 112,000 Iowans in digital skills through its Grow with Google partnerships.

The Council Bluffs campus has grown into one of Google's largest data center clusters globally over nearly two decades of continuous expansion, though Google's own public materials describe the campus in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

MidAmerican Energy, the principal electric utility serving Council Bluffs, has pursued a long-running commitment to source renewable wind generation for its Iowa customers, a factor Google has cited in its own public materials as part of the state's appeal for data center investment. Iowa's data center-specific sales tax exemption on qualifying equipment and electricity, administered at the state level, has been credited by state economic development officials with helping draw and retain large-scale data center investment in the state, including from Microsoft and Meta, both separately tracked in this registry.

profile.capacity_note: Google does not publish a megawatt IT capacity figure for any individual Council Bluffs building; third-party data center trackers (not Google's own disclosures) have estimated the overall Council Bluffs campus in the range of 100-300+ MW across its full build-out, a figure this entry does not adopt as fact because it is not operator-confirmed.
profile.facility_note: Google has not published a building-specific name, street address, or square footage for this individual structure within its Council Bluffs campus; this entry is one of the OSM-mapped buildings within that campus footprint, distinguished from its neighbors only by street (Vostok, McMurdo, Halley, Orcadas, Palmer, Concordia, or Bancroft Street) and coordinate.

reading.body:
This building is one of several structures within Google's Council Bluffs data center campus in Pottawattamie County, Iowa, mapped along Halley Street in Lewis Township. Google does not publish a megawatt capacity figure for this specific building or any individual structure at Council Bluffs. Third-party trackers estimate the overall campus at 100-300 MW, but this site does not adopt that figure as operator-confirmed fact. Google's own locations page describes the campus only in aggregate, not by address or building.

The Council Bluffs campus is Google's largest data center investment in Iowa and among its largest globally, opened in 2007 with an initial $600 million investment and now representing more than $20 billion of total state investment; Google announced a further $7 billion in 2025 shared between expanded Council Bluffs and a new Cedar Rapids facility. The campus qualifies for Iowa's data center-specific sales tax exemption on equipment and electricity. MidAmerican Energy serves the site and has pursued a long-running renewable wind commitment that Google has cited in public siting rationale.

Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities statewide, of which only 2 publish confirmed megawatt figures totaling 18 MW. The Council Bluffs campus ranks third by published megawatt capacity in the state, though its own published figure remains zero because Google does not disclose building- or campus-level capacity. Whether this facility matters to AI scaling depends on the unpublished watts it actually draws, a figure only Google and its grid operator hold.
